clue.text: Following lofty principles in trade, one's put in unlimited time

indicators.note: without its limits a word loses its first and last letters, keeping only the inside
something put in another thing ends up enclosed within it

blocks.note: the word with its two ends cut away
to trade is to deal
one is I, plus the 's

explanation.surface: Someone with high ideals spends a long time working in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited time' strips the clock word to its middle two letters, which then wrap the rest. 'One's' is read as I plus the 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealism is the pursuit of high principles, so someone following them is acting in a spirit of idealism.

clue.text: Artist's work crossing line, in a manner of speaking

definitions.note: describes the drawling manner of speech, used adjectivally

indicators.note: one thing crossing another has the second running through the middle of it

blocks.note: an artist produces a drawing
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A picture that has a line drawn across it, 'in a manner of speaking' suggesting a loose figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a throwaway hedge but is the definition, describing a style of talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, drawn-out way of talking, so drawling is literally a particular manner of speaking.

clue.text: Belligerent Nato is acting peculiarly

indicators.note: doing something peculiarly means doing it in an odd, disordered way, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: all twelve letters used

explanation.surface: The military alliance is behaving in an aggressive and odd fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonistic means actively hostile, which is close in sense to warlike or combative.

clue.text: In affair, one desperately pressed one's suit, perhaps

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: During a love affair, a lovesick suitor desperately pursued their courtship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressed one's suit' is the old phrase for wooing, which suits the affair; read literally, it means smoothing clothes with an iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing a suit of clothes flat with a hot iron is ironing it; 'perhaps' flags that a suit is only one example.

clue.text: People going over University's list of courses

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over means sitting above, so the first piece is placed on top

blocks.note: men are people
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Students reviewing the university's prospectus of degree courses.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'going over' means sitting above, so MEN comes before U.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu lists the dishes of a meal, which are served as courses; the university setting suggests academic courses instead.

clue.text: Feeling pain under military leader giving instruction

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed below, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: CO is a commanding officer
aching is feeling pain

explanation.surface: A soldier hurting under a harsh commander's drill.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts ACHING below CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaching is training or tutoring someone, which is a form of giving instruction.

clue.text: Graves, for example, that can be found in vault

definitions.text: that can be found in vault

blocks.note: first meaning: Graves is a Bordeaux region and its ...

blocks.clueFragment: that can be found in vault
blocks.note: second meaning: a vault is a cellar where bottles are stored

explanation.walkthrough: Graves and vault conjure a crypt full of burials; Graves is in fact a French wine district, and a wine vault is a cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a red or white Bordeaux, an example of the drink, and cellars or vaults are where such bottles are kept.

clue.text: In other words, visibly embarrassed about condition

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for the past participle: said again in other words

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first item wraps around the second

blocks.note: blushing shows embarrassment
a state is a condition

explanation.surface: Someone blushing as they rephrase something about their health.
explanation.walkthrough: Blushing red is the usual crossword sign of embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate something is to express it again, typically by putting it in other words.

clue.text: Stop possessions otherwise being covered by tax

indicators.note: something covered by another is wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: excise is a duty on goods
or as in 'or else'

explanation.surface: Seems to say belongings must be taxed or else seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possessions' means demonic possessions, not belongings; the tax here is the duty charged on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise is to drive out an evil spirit, ending a possession.

clue.text: Flat boat at stern of ship on river

indicators.note: in an across entry, A on B places A after B, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
aft means towards the back of a vessel

explanation.surface: A small flat vessel towed behind a ship on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' places A after B, so AFT follows R.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a simple flat floating platform used as a boat.

clue.text: At end of a new part of speech, stick declaration

indicators.note: at the end of means attached after, so the final piece follows everything else

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a noun is a part of speech
to cement is to stick fast

explanation.surface: Grammar talk: tack a declaration on to the end of a new part of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' is a grammar term here, not a section of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcement is a public statement, a formal declaration of news.

clue.text: Officer, as usual, supporting former PM

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece holds the other up from beneath, so it comes second

blocks.note: John Major was UK Prime Minister 1990 to 1997
in general means usually

explanation.surface: An army officer backing an ex-prime minister, as always.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts GENERAL beneath MAJOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A major general is a senior army rank, above brigadier and below lieutenant general.

clue.text: Senior investigator's command producing state of confusions

blocks.note: a DI is a Detective Inspector, plus the 's
an order is a command

explanation.surface: A police inspector's instruction causing a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorder is a lack of order, a confused or chaotic condition.

clue.text: Head of government, after financial disaster, in a sorry state?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: being ruined is financial collapse
first letter only

explanation.surface: A national leader left miserable after an economic crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts G behind RUIN. The question mark marks the playful definition: someone ruing is feeling sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret, so a person ruing something is sorry about it.

clue.text: Administer like high-fliers, including Conservative

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: high-fliers are in a jet
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory joins a group of high-flying administrators.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes into IN JET: IN-JE-C-T.
explanation.definitionFit: To inject a drug is to administer it by syringe.

clue.text: Fruit that's unlike peach, by the sound of it

indicators.note: tells us the word is identified by how it is pronounced, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: a peach is a beauty, so its opposite is plain-looking

explanation.surface: A comment comparing two fruits, one less attractive than a peach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peach' is slang for a lovely person, so unlike a peach is unattractive.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus hybrid, named for its wrinkled rind.

clue.text: Final is not altogether difficult — I'm at ease

indicators.note: not altogether means only part of the following words are used, the letters sitting within them

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word through the start of the last

explanation.surface: An exam candidate reflecting that the final paper was not too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means last in a series, the final one.

clue.text: Cast, getting fine fish

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
a ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler casts a line and lands a good fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling is to throw, and to cast is likewise to throw.

clue.text: Story with moral about weapon that's okay for fieldworker?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a fable is a tale that teaches a lesson
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: Evokes Animal Farm, an allegory with a moral about weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical definition: land fit for a farmer to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmable land is suitable for cultivation, so it is acceptable for someone who works the fields.

clue.text: Path travelled on horseback — or went by boat, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by its sound when spoken

blocks.clueFragment: travelled on horseback — or went by boat
blocks.note: both past tenses are pronounced the same way

explanation.surface: A route that someone covered on a horse, or else by rowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Either RODE or ROWED sounds the same as the answer, which is the point of the 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a way or track for travel, a path.

clue.text: A chap consuming steamed rice, as some Indians are

indicators.note: steamed food is cooked and broken down, so these letters are reworked
consuming means swallowing, so the second part goes inside the first

blocks.note: taken as written
a chap is a man
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man eating a plate of steamed rice, as many in India do.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indians meant are Native Americans, not people from India; the rice is the dish that misleads toward Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Native peoples of the Americas were long called American Indians, so some Indians are American.

clue.text: Formidable type that dentist can deal with

blocks.note: first meaning: a fierce, intimidating person
second meaning: hard deposit on the teeth

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a fearsome patient whom only a dentist can handle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a violent or ill-tempered person and the hard calcium crust scraped off teeth.

clue.text: Worked on plot, dreadfully deranged

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is done badly and messily, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone madly scheming over a plot like a deranged villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a scheme, but it is a patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To garden is to cultivate land, so someone who gardened worked on a plot of ground.

clue.text: Old master manages to swallow half of beer

indicators.note: half of a word means only one of its two halves is kept
swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
the first two of four letters

explanation.surface: An elderly boss succeeds in downing half a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old master' looks like a retired boss but means a great painter of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was a 17th-century Flemish painter, an old master in the art-history sense.

clue.text: Two kinds of seaman like hot cakes?

blocks.note: a merchant seaman serves in trading ships
an able seaman is a naval rank

explanation.surface: Sailors of two types being compared to hot cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both parts: merchant seaman and able seaman. Things that 'sell like hot cakes' sell easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchantable means fit to be sold, and hot cakes are the proverbial easy sellers.

clue.text: Right on time, turning up — excellent

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Arriving punctually, which is a fine thing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'R on ERA' puts R above ERA, which is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare can mean unusually good or fine, as in a rare treat.

clue.text: No-win situation stated in Asian language

indicators.note: stated means spoken, so the word is matched by its pronunciation

blocks.note: a tie is a draw, where no one wins

explanation.surface: A deadlock mentioned in an Asian tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai is the national language of Thailand in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Heap is what Pat may have dropped

indicators.note: what someone has dropped is the part they let fall away, here the bit left off a full name

blocks.note: Pat is a short form of the full first name

explanation.surface: Asks what an Irishman called Pat might have let fall onto a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: A man called Pat has dropped the end of PATRICK; that discarded end is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a stack of hay or straw, a kind of heap.

clue.text: Cultivate area on hill, producing food for Mexicans

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
to till is to plough the soil
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Farming a hillside patch to grow food for Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On hill' in an across clue puts the hill word first. A tor is a craggy hilltop, common on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is the thin maize flatbread that is a staple of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: One isn't perturbed about learner that's cheeky

indicators.note: perturbed means agitated and thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up
about means placed around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Someone calm about a learner driver who is being rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rudely disrespectful, and cheeky means impudent in the same way.
